Raspberries, as sold from frozen product, Poland retail/official control had lead higher at 45 µg/kg, against 12 µg/kg for fresh product, Poland retail/official control in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rusin M, Domagalska J, Rogala D, Razzaghi M, Szymala I · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Concentration of cadmium and lead in vegetables and fruits</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the raspberries came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

## What counts as raspberries

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers raspberries in 4 forms kept separate in every comparison: raspberries, as sold (129 results), raspberries, frozen (12 results), raspberries, dried (1 result) and raspberries, juice (1 <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-raspberries" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-raspberries-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of raspberries, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach raspberries

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach raspberries comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Raspberries, as sold from frozen product, Poland retail/official control had lead higher at 45 µg/kg, against 12 µg/kg for fresh product, Poland retail/official control in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rusin M, Domagalska J, Rogala D, Razzaghi M, Szymala I · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Concentration of cadmium and lead in vegetables and fruits</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

## Processing, cooking and preparation

<a id="hmi-ing-016"></a>
<a id="how-do-specified-processing-or-preparation-steps-change-the-measured-metal-endpoints"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-017"></a>

Processed or prepared forms were compared only with unprocessed raspberries in the same study and group. Raspberries, dried (PAHO) had lead higher at 10 µg/kg, against 7.65 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (raspberries, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, raspberries, frozen (all samples, market-share weighted) had Cu higher at 900 µg/kg, against 700 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (raspberries, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/zhang2017-red-raspberry-nutrient-profile|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Zhang X, Ahuja JKC, Burton-Freeman BM · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/zhang2017-red-raspberry-nutrient-profile">Characterization of the nutrient profile of processed red raspberries for use in nutrition labeling and promoting healthy food choices</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Nutrition and Healthy Aging</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/zhang2017-red-raspberry-nutrient-profile">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Forms differ in water content, so a per-kilogram difference is not by itself a measured removal or gain of metal.

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rusin M, Domagalska J, Rogala D, Razzaghi M, Szymala I · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Concentration of cadmium and lead in vegetables and fruits</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into raspberries?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, raspberries from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than raspberries from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rusin M, Domagalska J, Rogala D, Razzaghi M, Szymala I · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Concentration of cadmium and lead in vegetables and fruits</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Raspberries, as sold from frozen product, Poland retail/official control had lead higher at 45 µg/kg, against 12 µg/kg for fresh product, Poland retail/official control in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rusin M, Domagalska J, Rogala D, Razzaghi M, Szymala I · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Concentration of cadmium and lead in vegetables and fruits</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-raspberries" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-raspberries" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in raspberries?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in raspberries?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, raspberries, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (1.4 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (625 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For inorganic arsenic, the lowest regional median was in PAHO (11.8 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (77.5 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-raspberries" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-raspberries" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in raspberries?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in raspberries?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same raspberries.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Raspberries, dried (PAHO) had lead higher at 10 µg/kg, against 7.65 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (raspberries, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-raspberries-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-raspberries-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in raspberries is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in raspberries is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 4 results from 1 source, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> WHO GEMS/Food submissions reported inorganic arsenic in raspberries, as sold from 9 results in 2 reporting regions, with subgroup medians from 11.8 to 77.5 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
